hero.eyebrow: Small-batch keyboards, tuned before they ship
hero.tagline: A keyboard that feels finished on day one.
hero.subtitle: SIGNAL builds compact mechanical keyboards for people who type, edit, write, play, and notice when a switch sounds wrong. Every batch is assembled in small numbers, checked by hand, and shipped with practical options instead of mystery specs.
hero.proof1: Real keyboard photography, not product renders.
hero.proof2: Switches, stabilizers, and case fit checked before dispatch.
hero.proof3: Clear configuration notes before you pay.

products.heading: Three layouts. One careful build process.
products.subtitle: Choose the footprint first. We handle the switch feel, stabilizer work, and final desk-ready setup.

model60.name: Signal 60
model60.description: A compact build for small desks, travel kits, and focused writing. It keeps the essentials, drops the extra navigation cluster, and gives you more room for a mouse or notebook. Best for buyers who already know their shortcuts and want a board that disappears into the setup.

model75.name: Signal 75
model75.description: The balanced option for most desks. You get arrows, function keys, and a tighter footprint than a full-size board. We tune the stabilizers, check switch consistency, and ship it with a layout card so the first week feels familiar.

model100.name: Signal TKL
model100.description: A tenkeyless build for people who want a full navigation cluster without the numpad width. It is the easiest layout to recommend for mixed work: writing in the morning, spreadsheets after lunch, and games after hours.

tech.heading: Built like a workbench product, not a render.
tech.subtitle: The difference is in the last hour of assembly: switch seating, stabilizer noise, keycap alignment, and a typing test before the board goes into the box.
tech.imageAlt: Close-up of keyboard switches during a real mechanical keyboard build
tech.imageCaption: Each batch is checked on a physical board, with switches and stabilizers inspected before packaging.

feature1.title: Switch range
feature1.desc: For magnetic builds, we set practical actuation ranges and include the profile notes. For standard mechanical builds, we document the switch weight and feel clearly.

feature2.title: Saved setups
feature2.desc: Work, gaming, and quiet-hour profiles can be prepared before shipping. Nothing is locked: you can change the setup later.

feature3.title: Bench check
feature3.desc: Every finished unit rests and gets a second pass after assembly, so loose caps, rattly stabilizers, or obvious case issues are caught before dispatch.

customize.heading: Pick the parts that change the feel.
customize.subtitle: We keep the menu short on purpose. These are the choices that matter most once the keyboard is on your desk.
customize.imageAlt: Desk setup with a real custom keyboard on a work mat
customize.imageCaption: Configuration is practical: layout, switch feel, case material, and keycap profile.
